evidence: Confirmed in 01a6ab2 that horizon_reviewer_sha ran `gh api .../git/refs/tags/v1` on every pin-instrument.sh call, so verify-instrument.sh's two runs each resolved the moving tag independently; a tag move or a flaky API response between the two runs fails the byte-identical check for a reason that has nothing to do with the instrument. The agent resolved the sha once and threaded it into both runs via a new third positional.
guidance_note: A reproducibility test must resolve every externally-moving input exactly once and inject it into each run, decided when the test is written rather than when a reviewer points at the race.

evidence: Second thread on the same defect as F7: `gh api --jq '.content'` prints the literal string `null` at exit 0 when the Contents API omits content, and `null` is valid base64 alphabet, so the decode succeeds and the pipeline hashes garbage. The agent fixed both threads with one content-presence check in 01a6ab2's horizon_reviewer_prompt_sha256.
guidance_note: A `--jq` field extraction is an unchecked external call whenever the field can be JSON null; check for presence before the value reaches a decoder that accepts the string `null` as data.

evidence: Read verify-instrument.sh at 01a6ab2: the skills check was `local memento_skills=$WORK/run1/pinned/plugins/memento/skills`, the git-archive source dir, while README claimed the isolated config dir was what got verified. The reviewer's premise is exactly right and the agent moved the check onto installPath from `claude plugin list --json`.
guidance_note: A check meant to prove an installer wired something up must read the installer's own reported location, never the source directory the installer was handed.

evidence: Confirmed at 01a6ab2:51 the python heredoc asserted `ids == [memento@promptctl-horizon]` as a literal inside a script that sources lib.sh, where HORIZON_MARKETPLACE_NAME already declares that name. A rename in lib.sh would have made the acceptance check fail while reporting the instrument broken.
guidance_note: When a script sources a constants file, no literal in it may re-spell a constant that file owns - including inside embedded python or heredocs, which is exactly where the re-spelling hides from a grep of shell code.

evidence: Tested stock /usr/bin/base64 on the macOS this instrument runs on (Darwin 25.3): both `-d` and `-D` decode at exit 0, so the reviewer's specific claim that macOS breaks on `-d` is false today. The general BSD-portability concern is legitimate for older macOS and other BSDs, and the agent's capability probe is correct under either base64.
guidance_note: Run a portability claim against the actual target platform before accepting it; the right fix and a true premise are separate questions, and conceding a false premise is what teaches a reviewer to keep asserting it.

evidence: The reviewer hedged on whether v1 is annotated; the PR itself later settles it - the agent's F33 and F43 replies report the fixed code resolving v1 through the annotated-tag hop to commit 046cda2, so the original `.object.sha` would have recorded a tag-object sha and 404'd against the Contents API.
guidance_note: A refs/tags response's `.object.sha` is untyped until `.object.type` is read; resolve the type in the same call that fetches the sha rather than assuming a lightweight tag.

evidence: lib.sh's own header at 01a6ab2 claimed every external call is checked and aborts loudly with horizon_die, while horizon_reviewer_prompt_sha256 piped `--jq '.content'` straight into base64 with no presence check - the file contradicted its own stated invariant. The agent fixed F2 and F7 together with one check.
guidance_note: When a file header asserts an invariant like every external call is checked, audit each pipeline against that sentence before shipping the header - the header is the specification the reviewer will test you against.

evidence: Confirmed at 01a6ab2 lib.sh:39 and :49 that horizon_sha256_file and horizon_sha256_stdin each ran their own `command -v shasum` branch and the stdin variant dropped the `else horizon_die` arm, so a box with neither tool got a raw command-not-found instead of the clean message its sibling produced.
guidance_note: When two functions branch on the same capability probe, extract the selection in the first writing; a copied branch that silently drops the else arm is the default outcome of duplicating tool detection.

evidence: The relative path horizon/GOAL_PROMPT.md was typed once in pin-instrument.sh for the manifest's goal_wording.path field and again in lib.sh's horizon_goal_wording_sha256 to locate the bytes being hashed, so a move could leave the manifest recording a path the hash did not come from - which voids the manifest's own auditability claim.
guidance_note: A manifest field that records where a value came from must read that location from the same constant the code used to fetch it, or the record and the fetch can disagree silently.

evidence: goal_wording was the only one of four pinned identities read off the working tree while memento was pinned via git archive at a resolved sha and the reviewer prompt fetched at a resolved sha, so an uncommitted local edit produced a manifest value with no commit to audit it against - breaking pin-instrument.sh's own line-9 claim that every field resolves back to something checkable.
guidance_note: When a manifest claims every field is auditable, check each field's provenance against that claim before writing the claim; one working-tree read among git-pinned siblings is the field that falsifies it.

evidence: Read main() at 01a6ab2: it asserted plugin-list contents, absent CLAUDE.md and snapshot skill dirs, and nothing about memory, while both the script header and README enumerated `no owner memory` as a verified property. The stated acceptance criterion had no assertion behind it.
guidance_note: Write the assertions before writing the header that enumerates them; an enumerated criterion with no matching check is a PASS that proves less than the script says it does.

evidence: Duplicate of F4 - the reviewer posted the marketplace-name literal at verify-instrument.sh:51 twice under two thread ids. The premise is the same and correct; the agent fixed once and cross-referenced rather than editing twice.

horizon_repo_root at 01a6ab2 was a bare `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with no anchor, while both callers already computed SCRIPT_DIR from BASH_SOURCE to source lib.sh - so invoking the script by path from inside an unrelated repo would pin that repo instead. The reviewer's fix (pass the anchor in) is what the agent did.
guidance_note: A script that computes SCRIPT_DIR to find its own library must use the same anchor to find its repo; resolving the repo from the process CWD makes what the script operates on a property of the caller.

evidence: Duplicate of F13 raised at the pin-instrument.sh call site rather than at lib.sh's definition; same root cause, same fix, and the agent said so and fixed once.

The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT ef35b67 flag is a false positive: I read README.md and lib.sh at 01a6ab2 and both spellings were already there - README:34 `dev build, build date unknown` against lib.sh's `dev build (build date unknown)`. The drift predates every fix; the reviewer simply did not reach the README in round 0.
guidance_note: Transcribe an external tool's output in exactly one file; a second transcription in a doc has already drifted from the first by the time anyone compares them.

evidence: The flag is a false positive on this line: `memento_ref=$(git -C $repo_root rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)` is at 01a6ab2 pin-instrument.sh:47, unchanged by ef35b67 except for the repo_root anchor. It was the one git call outside lib.sh, contradicting lib.sh's own header, and horizon_resolve_memento_ref already accepted a bare HEAD so the call bought nothing.
guidance_note: Before writing a header that claims a library owns every invocation of a tool, grep the sibling scripts for that tool - the claim is only as true as the last script anyone edited.

evidence: ef35b67's fix for F3 replaced the snapshot-dir skills check with one reading installPath from `claude plugin list --json`, but never asserted that path falls under $config_dir - so the new check proved the skills exist somewhere, which is not the isolation property F3 was raised about. The fix moved the check without restoring what it was supposed to prove.
guidance_note: When a fix relocates a proof onto a path an external tool reports, assert that path is inside the boundary being proven in the same edit, or the replacement proves no more than what it replaced.

evidence: ef35b67 added the third [reviewer-sha] positional to pin-instrument.sh as F1's fix and left README's synopsis at `<run-dir> [memento-ref]` plus its unconditional byte-identical claim - so the doc described a command signature that no longer existed and promised reproducibility the code now says requires the new argument.
guidance_note: A fix that changes a script's argument list is not finished until the README synopsis and every claim that depends on those arguments have been re-read in the same edit.

evidence: False positive on the flag: `horizon_lit_sha256() { horizon_sha256_file $(horizon_lit_path); }` sits at 01a6ab2 lib.sh:125-126 untouched by ef35b67. The nested substitution's exit is discarded when used as an argument, so a missing lit produced horizon_die's message plus an unrelated empty-filename error from the hasher.
guidance_note: Never nest a function that can exit inside another call's argument list - capture it into a checked assignment, because a command substitution's exit status is discarded in argument position and set -e never sees it.

evidence: The `[ -d $config_dir/projects ]` assertion was new code from ef35b67's F11 fix. The reviewer's hypothesised install-time projects/ bookkeeping is speculative and the agent's reply says it confirmed empirically that no projects/ dir is created today, so the predicted false failure is not real - but the check genuinely was broader than the comment above it, which located memory at projects/*/memory/.
guidance_note: Write an assertion at the exact granularity the comment beside it claims; a broader proxy for the real condition is a false failure waiting for the external tool to add unrelated bookkeeping.

evidence: False positive on the flag: `ref=$(git -C $repo_root rev-parse HEAD)` is at 01a6ab2 verify-instrument.sh:28, present before any fix. It is the same contract violation as F16 in the other script, and only the pin-instrument.sh instance was flagged in round 0.
guidance_note: When a library header claims sole ownership of a tool, write every entry-point script against that contract at once rather than fixing the one script the reviewer named.

evidence: Verified at 01a6ab2 that verify-instrument.sh's main() opens straight into repo_root and the raw git call with no horizon_need block at all, while pin-instrument.sh preflighted git/gh/claude/python3 - so a missing git or gh gave a raw command-not-found in one script and a clean die in its sibling. Both halves of this finding are original-code defects, not fix residue.
guidance_note: Give every entry-point script the same preflight block when the first one is written; a second script that sources the same library but skips the preflight has the library's error convention only by accident.

evidence: False positive on the e09f519 flag: `plugin_list=$(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$config_dir claude plugin list --json)` is at 01a6ab2 verify-instrument.sh:45 with no `|| fail`, in a script that defines fail() precisely to make its diagnostics uniform. Real but cosmetic - the script still aborts, just with raw CLI output.
guidance_note: When a script defines a fail() to make its output uniform, route every external call through it in the first writing; the one call that does not is the one that fires in CI.

evidence: The unwrapped install_path extraction is new code from ef35b67's F3 fix (the recorded_lit_sha256 extraction beside it was original at 01a6ab2:65), and neither routed through fail(), so a schema change surfaced as a raw Python traceback. The agent's extra deletion of `[ -n $install_path ]` is sound: python either prints a path or dies into the new `|| fail`, and an empty path would fail the later under-config-dir prefix match anyway.
guidance_note: Code written to fix a finding must adopt the file's existing error convention in the same edit; a new external call that skips the file's `|| fail` is a fresh review round the fix paid for.

evidence: Grepped README at 01a6ab2: the sentence `Everything except the reviewer is a pure function of memento-ref` is absent, so e09f519 wrote it as F18's fix. It is false for lit, whose sha256 comes from `command -v lit` at call time, and the paragraph four lines below already conceded exactly that by calling a changed lit hash real config drift.
guidance_note: When rewriting a doc claim about what is reproducible, enumerate every field the claim quantifies over against the code that produces each one, instead of asserting the set boundary from memory.

evidence: False positive on the flag: both asserts are at 01a6ab2 verify-instrument.sh:51-52. The defect is real and the agent reproduced it - under PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 the heredoc exits 0 on empty input, so the script printed PASS having checked nothing, voiding its own header claim that exit 0 means the criteria held. The agent then mutation-tested the sys.exit replacement under the same flag.
guidance_note: Never implement an acceptance check with a Python assert; assertions have an off switch the script does not control, so the check can be disabled by an environment the script never sees.

evidence: The `case $install_path in $config_dir/*` prefix match is new code from e09f519's F17 fix, and the agent reproduced the divergence on the macOS box this runs on (/var/folders/... vs /private/var/folders/...). Rather than canonicalizing at the comparison as the reviewer suggested, it canonicalized WORK once at creation so every derived path is canonical from one place, and realpath'd install_path on the other side.
guidance_note: A path comparison added as a fix must canonicalize at the point the paths are created, on any platform where /var or /tmp is a symlink - repairing each comparison as it is found is how one canonicalization bug becomes several.

evidence: The agent's own reply names the cause: `this is a leftover from my own previous edit`. 7eee5da's F25 fix moved lit into the externally-resolved bucket and left the closing sentence still promising a fully byte-identical manifest from pinning memento-ref plus reviewer-sha, which a lit upgrade mid-campaign breaks.
guidance_note: After moving an item between two categories in a doc, re-read every downstream sentence that quantifies over either category before pushing - the sentence that names the categories is rarely the only one that depends on them.

evidence: False positive on the flag: `lit_path=$(horizon_lit_path)` and `lit_sha256=$(horizon_lit_sha256)` are at 01a6ab2 pin-instrument.sh:65-66, and horizon_lit_sha256 calls horizon_lit_path internally, so the manifest's binary_path and sha256 came from two independent `command -v lit` resolutions that nothing bound together.
guidance_note: Two record fields that jointly identify one artifact must come from one resolution of that artifact; a helper that re-resolves internally is a second resolution however convenient its name.

evidence: False positive on the flag: the sentence attributing all three isolation properties to the marketplace is at 01a6ab2 README:31-33. The reviewer is right on the mechanism - horizon_provision_config_dir does `rm -rf` then `mkdir -p` before the marketplace is registered, so CLAUDE.md and memory absence come from an empty dir, and only plugin isolation is the marketplace's doing.
guidance_note: When one sentence attributes several properties to one mechanism, verify each property against the code that produces it; a sentence that over-attributes invites a later change that silently drops the property it never covered.

evidence: Read e09f519's pin-instrument.sh patch: F19's fix added exactly one line, `horizon_need lit`, and swept no further - leaving tar, reached from `git archive | tar -x` inside lib.sh, unchecked, so pipefail attributed a missing tar to the `git archive` die message. The reviewer explicitly names the lit-preflight fix as the precedent.
guidance_note: When adding one tool to a preflight list, enumerate every external command reachable from the library's pipelines and add them all in that edit; adding the one the reviewer named guarantees the next round.

evidence: The mktemp/git-show/rm structure does not exist at 01a6ab2 - horizon_goal_wording_sha256 hashed the working-tree file directly - so ef35b67's F10 fix created both the temp file and the leak, and the agent reproduced it (`LEAKED (rm was skipped)`). The unguarded hash aborts under the caller's set -e before reaching rm.
guidance_note: A fix that introduces a temp file owes it a cleanup arm on every exit path in the same edit; guarding only the failure the fix was written for is how a correctness fix ships a resource leak.

evidence: 01a6ab2's horizon_reviewer_sha was a correctly checked `gh api ... --jq '.object.sha' || horizon_die`; ef35b67's F6 fix replaced it with `read -r sha type < <(gh api ...)`, where the `||` observes read's status rather than gh's. The agent reproduced a producer that emits a full line then exits 1 slipping straight past the check and printing a non-commit sha as the pin.
guidance_note: Never put a command whose failure matters inside a process substitution - capture into a checked assignment and read from a here-string, because `read` reports only its own status and a partially-written line makes it succeed.

evidence: ef35b67's F1 fix added the reviewer-sha override, and verify-instrument.sh supplies it on both runs, so the common case writes `tag: v1` beside a resolved_sha that was never checked against that tag - the manifest implying a resolution that did not happen. The agent recorded a discriminated reviewer.resolved_from value rather than the reviewer's suggested boolean.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a way to supply a value that was previously derived, the record of that value must state which path produced it, or the record keeps asserting a relationship the new path never establishes.

evidence: Same gap as F31 in the same preflight list: e09f519's F19 fix added only `horizon_need lit`, and base64 - invoked by horizon_base64_decode_stdin inside the reviewer-prompt pipeline - stayed unchecked, so a minimal image reports a raw command-not-found instead of horizon_die.
guidance_note: One enumeration of the library's pipelines catches tar and base64 together; discovering the tool set one reviewer round at a time is the cost being measured here.

evidence: The manifest-writing python heredoc is original (01a6ab2 pin-instrument.sh:78-116, unwrapped), so the line is not fix-authored; the finding exists because 7eee5da's F24 fix wrapped the two python calls in verify-instrument.sh and did not sweep the sibling python call in the other script. The agent's reply also self-reports catching a dead `[ $? -eq 0 ]` first attempt before pushing.
guidance_note: When a fix establishes an error-reporting convention for one class of call, apply it to every call of that class across the PR's whole diff in the same edit, not just the file the reviewer was reading.

evidence: a5e25f5's fix for F31/F35 added `horizon_need tar` and `horizon_need base64` and stopped there, leaving awk - which lib.sh:55 and :61 pipe every hash through, so every pinned identity depends on it - unchecked. This is the third consecutive round spent extending the same preflight list one tool at a time.
guidance_note: Derive the preflight list mechanically from the commands the library actually invokes rather than from the ones a reviewer has named so far; the list is a fact about the code, not a growing accumulation of review findings.

evidence: Read a5e25f5's lib.sh patch: F32's fix wrapped horizon_sha256_file inside horizon_goal_wording_sha256 in a checked assignment with horizon_die, and left the identical call in horizon_lit_sha256 - created by e09f519's F19 fix, sixty lines up in the same file - bare. Same primitive, same commit, unswept.
guidance_note: When wrapping one call to a shared primitive, grep for the primitive and wrap every call site in that edit; a convention applied at one site is a convention the next reviewer round will find broken at the others.

evidence: False positive on the a5e25f5 flag: the comment `shasum on macOS, sha256sum elsewhere` and the presence-based `if command -v shasum` beneath it are both at 01a6ab2 lib.sh:37-39, and a5e25f5's lib.sh patch touches only horizon_reviewer_sha and horizon_goal_wording_sha256. The comment was never true - ef35b67 merely hoisted it above the extracted helper.
guidance_note: A comment that names platforms must match the branch it sits above; describe the condition the code tests (presence) rather than the reason you expect that condition to hold (OS).

evidence: Checked the agent's counter-claim against memento's address-pr-reviews SKILL.md: its Finalize section runs `gh pr merge --squash` and `lit done` and explicitly forbids punting to a human, so the reviewer's `the loop as written never integrates completed work` is wrong. The wording defect is real - GOAL_PROMPT.md's terminus was `until the PR is clean and mergeable. Then return to lit`, one step short of its own loop summary. GOAL_PROMPT.md is untouched by a5e25f5, so the flag is also a false positive.
guidance_note: When a prompt delegates a step to a named skill, state the end state that skill delivers rather than the step before it; a terminus one step short of the skill's own is where a literal reader stops.

evidence: Confirmed in a5e25f5's lib.sh patch that F33's fix hardened the first gh call into a checked tsv parse with non-empty assertions and left the dereference hop's bare `--jq '.object.sha'` three lines below untouched, where jq prints the literal `null` at exit 0. The agent extracted one horizon_gh_object boundary both calls go through instead of adding a third null check.
guidance_note: When hardening one call to an external API, harden every call in the same function in that edit; the sibling three lines down is precisely what the next round finds.

evidence: Duplicate of F37 - the reviewer raised the missing `horizon_need awk` twice on pin-instrument.sh:55 under two thread ids. Same cause: a5e25f5's tar/base64 preflight fix did not sweep the awk in lib.sh's hash pipelines.

ef35b67's F6 fix dereferenced exactly one hop and trusted the result, so a tag object pointing at another tag object would put a non-commit sha into reviewer.resolved_sha. The agent's justification for leaving the loop unbounded is sound - a git tag object's content includes its target sha, so a cycle would require the sha to be known before it is computed - and it added a terminal `commit` type assertion the reviewer did not ask for.
guidance_note: A dereference over a self-similar structure must loop and then assert the terminal type; handling one hop delivers less than the function's name promises and the second hop is representable.

narrative: A 608-line, five-file bash instrument drew 43 findings across five reviewing rounds before hitting the round cap. Rounds 1 through 4 each still contained findings on lines untouched since 01a6ab2 (F15/F16/F19/F21/F22, F23/F26, F29/F30/F36, F39/F40), so no round is cleanly attributable to the agent's own fixes - the reviewer kept finding original defects it had missed earlier. Eighteen of the 43, though, exist only because an earlier fix was incomplete: F6's tag-dereference fix alone spawned F33, F41 and F43, and F3's installPath fix spawned F17, F27, F24 and F36. The agent's judgment was uniformly sound - every accept was warranted, it reproduced the defect before fixing on at least six threads and mutation-tested three fixes, and on F40 it checked the address-pr-reviews skill and correctly contradicted the reviewer's premise while still fixing the wording. What cost rounds was sweep discipline, not judgment: three separate classes (preflight tools, `|| fail` wrappers, README claims) were each fixed one instance per round.
guidance_observations: Three of the five rounds were driven by fixes applied at exactly the instance the reviewer named - preflight tools arrived one per round (lit, then tar+base64, then awk), external-call wrappers one file per round, and README claims one sentence per round.

Four fixes introduced a defect the next round found (F6 to F33 and F43, F10 to F32, F3 to F17), all in newly written code that did not adopt the file's own existing error-handling or proof convention.

Verify-before-fix was the strongest habit in this PR - the agent reproduced PYTHONOPTIMIZE assert stripping, the macOS /var symlink divergence, the temp-file leak, and the process-substitution read escape before touching code, and none of those accepts was wrong; the gap was breadth of sweep, not depth of check.
Two finding pairs were the reviewer posting the same issue twice on one line (F4/F12, F37/F42); the agent fixed once and cross-referenced the sibling thread, which is correct and cost nothing.

The PR hit MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS at round 5 and merged with the head commit unreviewed, so 08c0ff8 - which rewrote horizon_reviewer_sha into a new horizon_gh_object boundary and looped the tag dereference - shipped with no review at all.
